description: The article distinguishes disturbing methods (questionnaires interrupting game-play) from non-disturbing methods that monitor engagement \"without interrupting the game-play and game flow\".
title: Non-disturbing engagement monitoring via game-play interaction logging and physiological sensing

description: The article adapts Campbell and Stanley's nonequivalent control group design to standalone library instruction: treatment and control sections are pre-existing course sections rather than individually randomized, and an in-class pretest strengthens evidence that the groups are similar.
title: Nonequivalent control group quasi-experimental design

description: A fully disaggregated nonlinear Bayesian mixed-effects model, implemented in the R package brms, estimating each participant's initial accuracy, rate of change (a time constant), and asymptotic accuracy as a continuous function of trial number, with an exponential change curve bounded via logistic-r
title: Nonlinear mixed-effects Bayesian learning-curve modeling

description: The study applies normalisation process theory (NPT) as a theoretical lens for exploring enablers and barriers to integrating IVR simulation into routine practice.
title: Normalisation Process Theory (NPT)

title: Normative four-criterion framework for visualizing meta-analytic clearinghouse evidence for decision-making
